courseDescriptionInputs.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

readerValues.programmeDescription: Leiden Medicine combines the biological basis of health and disease with clinical problems, patient communication, physical examination, scientific inquiry and professional development. Supervised care experience and longitudinal skills teaching connect medical knowledge with patient care.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: This qualified academic-core comparison assesses the documented first 120 EC. UCR can combine substantive biomedical mechanisms and disease-case reasoning with patient perspectives, psychological interviewing and evidence-based inquiry. It does not reproduce physician physical examination, BLS, supervised care placements or longitudinal medical-skills assessment, including those already required in the first two years. All third-year study and final work are outside the comparison; this is not equivalent medical training.

curriculum.limitation: The inventory contains 173 documented EC: 120 EC from the first two years and 53 EC of listed third-year requirements and restricted choice. Seven EC remain unallocated and are not assigned to LPV3 by subtraction. Only the first-two-year academic core is compared. All 60 EC of third-year study and final work, including the listed 53 EC and 15-EC restricted half-minor, are outside the claim. The 2-EC Planetary Health title and weight are known, but its detailed content is unverified. Full cohort progression and graduation are not certified.

componentNotes.y3-half-minor: A 15-EC restricted faculty half-minor selection, outside the assessed core. It is not unrestricted free choice; current approval, access and endpoint conditions remain unverified.
componentNotes.y1-3011int00y: Medicine-specific orientation includes competencies, study preparation and patient perspectives. The UCR program has its own academic introduction and PPD; these are not the same requirement.
componentNotes.y1-3011vgtj1y: An integrated adaptive medical-knowledge progress examination with reflection in a portfolio. The UCR program uses course assessments instead.
componentNotes.y1-ba-gen-yr1-thema: A credited package including healthcare orientation and AI/technology themes. UCR evidence and health study offers context, but no dedicated equivalent package is assumed.

componentNotes.y2-30123pd10y: The current catalogue confirms the 2-EC title and allocation, but supplies no detailed description. Its specific content and correspondence remain unverified.
componentNotes.y2-30125bu10y: The dedicated abdominal block integrates differential diagnosis, treatment plans, prosection, imaging and patient demonstrations. UCR has relevant anatomy and disease-case reasoning, but not this complete clinical teaching arrangement.
componentNotes.y2-3012vgtj2y: A further integrated medical-knowledge progress examination, with its own assessment and reflection requirements.
componentNotes.y2-30126bw00y: The dedicated locomotion block requires clinical reasoning from history, physical findings and examination across orthopedic, rheumatic and neurological problems. UCR does not reproduce this integrated clinical block.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic-core comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The documented first- and second-year 120-EC core, including its known biological, clinical-problem, patient-care and evidence requirements. Specific correspondence for the unpublished 2-EC Planetary Health description is withheld.
comparisonScope.excluded: All third-year 60 EC and final work, including 53 EC of listed study and restricted half-minor choice plus 7 EC not yet allocated. Full cohort access, progression, graduation and equivalent clinical or professional training are not certified.

cellNotes.text: Both study molecular and cellular mechanisms and connect them to disease and intervention. UCR develops cell regulation, molecular drug mechanisms and research appraisal; the exact integrated medical cases differ.

Both relate human anatomical structure to function using spatial reasoning and medical images. UCR includes specimens and surface anatomy; the full medical histology, embryology and patient-demonstration integration is not reproduced.

Both examine integrated organ function, homeostasis and physiological regulation, including cardiovascular, respiratory and renal systems. UCR is a wider physiology course; the medical block and its clinical examples have a different organization.

Both connect biochemical processes and metabolic regulation to health and disease. UCR emphasizes pathways, enzymes and biochemical disease mechanisms; Leiden adds a dedicated endocrine, reproductive and nutritional clinical sequence.

Both study nervous-system anatomy, physiology and dysfunction. UCR uses comparative neurobiology, behavior and disorder research; the dedicated medical neuroanatomy, imaging and clinical examination context remains different.

Both analyze infection, immune responses, inflammation and immunopathology in clinical and mechanistic contexts. UCR adds flow-cytometry analysis and research synthesis; the full medical diagnostic and treatment sequence differs.

Both examine cellular and genetic pathology, neoplasia and disease mechanisms. UCR develops molecular diagnosis, genetic ethics and research proposals; the detailed tumor-treatment and hemodynamic case sequence is not identical.

Both study drug targets, pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics with quantitative reasoning. UCR uses response models, virtual experiments and research design; this does not confer clinical prescribing or reproduce every patient-specific calculation.

Both use organ-system mechanisms and diagnostic findings to reason through cardiovascular, respiratory and renal clinical cases. UCR works with published cases across several systems; it does not reproduce the dedicated patient-based thorax and kidney block.

Both develop research questions, study designs, data analysis and scientific reporting. UCR uses actual empirical projects and R; Leiden integrates research with care-placement data and medical academic formation.

Both develop research-design knowledge, statistical analysis and evidence appraisal. UCR supplies applied multivariable and experimental methods; the full clinical-research package and its medical integration remain different.

Both address patient perspectives, health behavior, medical consultation and communication. UCR includes interviewing practice and health-case formulation; it does not supply BLS, physician physical examination, supervised care or longitudinal medical-skills certification.

Both develop introductory clinical interviewing, assessment and reflective skills. UCR focuses on psychological assessment and psychotherapy; physician consultation, physical examination and the medical portfolio and skills tests remain distinct.

Both address prevention and health promotion using evidence and patient or population contexts. UCR adds epidemiological designs and a local health project; the package’s specific medical-law and professional-ethics teaching is not replaced.
